2016.emphasis_summary: Anchored in say-on-pay support history (95% in 2015, 96% in 2014) and stockholder-engagement feedback on the compensation program, with patient-safety and product-quality commitments; the human-capital and diversity sections are blank.
2016.notable_shifts: First available year in sample; no prior-year comparison.

2017.emphasis_summary: Reports 2016 say-on-pay support of 94% and explains that the compensation peer group was simplified into the AbbVie Health Care Peer Group, with long-term incentive design as the main compensation topic.
2017.notable_shifts: Reported say-on-pay support slips from 95% to 94%, and long-term incentive references rise from nine to 16. The peer group is simplified, while environmental and climate language remains almost absent (one environment mention).

2018.emphasis_summary: Introduces substantial environmental and social content, including a CDP A- climate score, Dow Jones Sustainability Index leadership, workforce diversity recognition and a human-rights commitment.
2018.notable_shifts: Environmental references go from one to 19 and emissions references from zero to 16 for the first time, while the compensation-program language recedes (long-term incentive references fall from 16 to two). Women-related and human-rights references also appear (four and five mentions).

2019.emphasis_summary: Highlights a women-in-management push (47% of management positions globally held by women) with a new Women's Leadership Program, plus human-rights and occupational-safety recognition from the Dow Jones Sustainability Index.
2019.notable_shifts: Women-related references surge from four to 15 and emissions references drop from 16 to zero, while peer-group discussion peaks at eight mentions (from one).

2020.emphasis_summary: Focuses on COVID-19 (a virtual annual meeting for stockholder safety), responsible drug-pricing commitments, and a broad clawback authority to recover incentive-plan awards.
2020.notable_shifts: Drug-pricing references jump from two to 10 and COVID-19 appears for the first time (one mention), while women-related mentions fall from 15 to six.

2021.emphasis_summary: Centers on the COVID-19 response (including the NIH-led ACTIV partnership), publication of the EEO-1 report, board diversity data, and expanded anti-hedging and clawback language.
2021.notable_shifts: COVID-19 references surge from one to 23 and anti-hedging references jump from two to eight, while drug-pricing references fall from 10 to zero.

2022.emphasis_summary: Describes an environmental sustainability strategy built on reducing the company's environmental footprint and growing sustainably, with an expanded clawback description, board diversity data and rising majority-voting and proxy-access references.
2022.notable_shifts: Sustainability references nearly triple (eight to 23) and environment references jump from one to 12 in the human-capital excerpt, while COVID-19 references drop from 23 to zero.

2023.emphasis_summary: Points to the ESG Action Report and 2023 ESG highlights, and frames environmental strategy as reducing footprint and growing sustainably through innovation, with clawback and board diversity data.
2023.notable_shifts: Greenhouse-gas and carbon-target language appears (two mentions, from zero) and emissions references return (two, from zero), while the broader sustainability-strategy language stays roughly flat at 24 mentions.

2024.emphasis_summary: Centers on the ESG Action Report's alignment with the UN Sustainable Development Goals and SASB, a board-diversity and EEO-1 workforce overview, and majority-voting, clawback and anti-hedging policies.
2024.notable_shifts: Majority-voting references jump from seven to 20 and clawback references rise from three to six, while sustainability mentions fall from 24 to 13 and greenhouse-gas target language drops from two to one.
